clue.text: Fellow feeling bird — jump, for pity's sake!

definitions.note: a jump is slang for a sexual encounter; one had out of pity is the answer

parts.note: sympathy is literally feeling with a fellow creature
a shag is a seabird of the cormorant family

explanation.surface: An exclamation of exasperation about a bird jumping, said with fellow feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird and the jump look like one picture, but the bird is wordplay and the jump belongs to the definition; shag is British slang for having sex as well as the bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexual encounter granted out of pity rather than desire is what the slang phrase describes.

clue.text: See 1
Be most excited getting head from Robin Hood

definitions.note: a hood, or hoodlum, is a gangster

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: these two words are used letter by letter

indicators.note: the head of Robin's name is its first letter

parts.note: the outlaw's first name supplies its initial

explanation.surface: Getting oral sex from Robin Hood is the most exciting thing imaginable.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin Hood reads as the outlaw, but the two names split: Robin gives a letter and Hood is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hood is short for hoodlum, a violent criminal or gangster.

clue.text: Protected species of member, a penis substitute long having replaced date

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
taken as written

indicators.note: one letter takes the place of another in the sex toy

parts.note: a dildo is a sex toy shaped like a penis

explanation.surface: A smutty tale of a member, a sex toy, and a long one standing in for a date.
explanation.walkthrough: Protected is a joke: the armadillo is armoured, not under legal protection.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is a species of mammal shielded by a bony shell, so naturally protected.

clue.text: Chart-topping performer? He'll slay 'em!

definitions.meaning: first meaning, punning: a man with a hit record

explanation.walkthrough: Slaying an audience means wowing it, so both halves seem to praise a star; the second is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitman is a contract killer, while read as hit plus man it suggests a hit-making singer.

clue.text: Useless type, 'Pudding Brenda'

parts.note: duff is an old British word for a boiled pudding, as in plum duff
Private Eye calls the Queen Brenda, so she is ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A sneering nickname for a hopeless person, Pudding Brenda.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's long-running nickname for Queen Elizabeth II, which makes her ER here.
explanation.definitionFit: A duffer is an incompetent, ineffectual person, a fair synonym for someone hopeless.

clue.text: Stimulant making a meal pointless?

indicators.note: a compass point, S for south, is dropped from the meal

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A pick-me-up that renders a dinner pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: An upper is slang for a stimulant drug such as amphetamine.

clue.text: Figure out about Blair's number one being incendiary type

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the leader's initial
the letters of figure are worked out into a new order

parts.note: the word figure is used letter by letter

indicators.note: the number one of Blair's name is its first letter

parts.note: the Prime Minister's surname supplies its initial

explanation.surface: Working out the inflammatory character of Blair's number one, the Prime Minister himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Figure out reads as a phrasal verb, but out signals the shuffle of figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A firebug is an arsonist, someone who starts fires, so an incendiary person.

clue.text: Explosive put under Brenda, say, as the queen gets to eat?

definitions.text: as the queen gets to eat?

indicators.note: in a down entry the explosive is placed below the royal

parts.note: Private Eye's Brenda, the Queen, is an example of a royal
jelly is slang for gelignite

explanation.surface: A plot to put a bomb under the Queen, dressed up as her dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The queen of the definition is a queen bee, not Brenda.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal jelly is the secretion worker bees feed to larvae that will become queen bees.

clue.text: Delirious etc, about arse of highly fanciable type

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the backside
the letters of etc are jumbled, as if in a frenzy

parts.note: the abbreviation is used letter by letter
the rump is the buttocks

explanation.surface: Going wild over the bottom of someone very attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: Crumpet is British slang for attractive people collectively, as well as a teatime bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Crumpet is British slang for a sexually desirable person, someone found very attractive.

clue.text: Clinton's one-time vice — "fanny", for the record

parts.note: Al Gore was Bill Clinton's vice president
fanny is American slang for the backside, which is a bum

explanation.surface: A smutty aside about one of Bill Clinton's weaknesses, put on the record.
explanation.walkthrough: Vice suggests one of Clinton's habits, but it is his vice president, Al Gore. In British use fanny is a much ruder word than the American one meaning bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a long-playing record, a collection of tracks issued together.

clue.text: Try to pray for rehabilitation of this unpopular lot!

indicators.note: rehabilitation remakes something, so the letters of the phrase are rebuilt into a new order

parts.note: these three words are used letter by letter

explanation.surface: A jibe that the unpopular Conservatives must pray if they are ever to be rehabilitated.
explanation.definitionFit: The Conservatives were deeply unpopular in 2005, after years out of office under Tony Blair's Labour government.

clue.text: Just the place for nags to get laid and boss husband

definitions.text: Just the place for nags to get laid

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud on a surface
to husband land is to manage and cultivate it, that is, to farm it

explanation.surface: A boss and her husband settle on the ideal spot for horses to mate.
explanation.walkthrough: Boss and husband look like people, but boss is a raised knob and husband is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud farm is where horses are kept for breeding, so where mares are covered.

clue.text: Blair's head in spin — he doesn't welcome this sort

indicators.note: the leader's initial is placed inside the word for spin

parts.note: to reel is to whirl or spin round

indicators.note: the head of Blair's name is its first letter

parts.note: the Prime Minister's surname supplies its initial

explanation.surface: A Labour backbencher who has no time for Blair's spin doctoring.
explanation.walkthrough: Spin suggests New Labour's media management, but here it is a whirling motion.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebel resists authority, so he does not welcome the leadership's line or its spin.

clue.text: Fertility rating of Dracula, maybe, after sulphur put on hairdo

indicators.note: in a down entry the sulphur symbol sits on top of the hairdo
the vampire's title follows the sulphur and the hairdo

parts.note: a perm is a permanent wave in the hair
Dracula is a count, a nobleman's title

explanation.surface: A vampire's virility measured after he gets a sulphurous perm.
explanation.definitionFit: A sperm count measures sperm concentration, a key gauge of male fertility.

clue.text: Over-elaborate royal habit

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the colour of robes worn by emperors and kings

explanation.surface: A sniping remark about the monarchy's fussy, overdone customs.
explanation.walkthrough: Habit looks like a custom, but it is clothing, the robes of royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Purple prose is overwrought writing, and purple has long been the dye of imperial and royal garments.

clue.text: Rather too casual gent removed — wow! — flimsy female wear

indicators.note: the man is taken away from the longer word for careless

parts.note: negligent means careless, too casual about things
the word gent itself, which sits inside the longer word
gee is an exclamation of surprise, like wow

explanation.surface: A gentleman steps out, and wow, there's a flimsy nightdress on show.
explanation.definitionFit: A negligee is a light, often sheer, dressing gown or nightgown worn by women.

clue.text: Blair, lacking bar skill is a hindrance

indicators.note: Blair goes without the letters of bar, which are taken out of it

parts.note: ability means skill

explanation.surface: A jibe that Tony Blair, short of courtroom talent, is a burden.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking B, A and R out of BLAIR leaves LI. Blair trained as a barrister, so 'bar skill' reads as legal talent.
explanation.definitionFit: A liability is a person or thing that causes trouble or puts others at a disadvantage.

clue.text: Having a wee drink, up and confess

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the drink is read from the bottom

parts.note: to sip is to drink a little
to sing is slang for confessing to the police

explanation.surface: A wee drink, then bottoms up and own up.
explanation.walkthrough: Wee looks like the Scottish word for small, qualifying the drink; it is urination.
explanation.definitionFit: Pissing is the coarse word for urinating, which is what having a wee means.

clue.text: Hot air produced by right-hand, erotic manipulation

parts.note: R and H are standard abbreviations for right and hand

indicators.note: manipulating the letters works them into a new arrangement

parts.note: the word erotic is used letter by letter

explanation.surface: Smutty talk of erotic handiwork turns out to be nothing but empty words.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetoric used dismissively means grand but empty talk, which is what hot air describes.

clue.text: E-bay's involved with M&S's disastrous 'mission'

indicators.note: the letters are tangled together
a disastrous mixture jumbles both brands' letters

parts.note: the auction site's name with its 's, used letter by letter
M&S is Marks & Spencer, the British department store

explanation.surface: An online auction site teaming up with Marks & Spencer on a doomed mission.
explanation.walkthrough: M&S is Marks & Spencer, a British high-street store.
explanation.definitionFit: An embassy is a diplomatic mission, the delegation sent by one state to another.

clue.text: A tumble's good in the morning with hairless bollocks

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, marks the morning

indicators.note: the hair, locks, is shaved off the end of the word bollocks

parts.note: the word itself, a British slang term for testicles

explanation.surface: A morning romp in bed, with the man freshly shaved below.
explanation.walkthrough: Hairless works literally on the word: bollocks loses its locks.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambol is a playful leap or frolic, close to a tumble in the sense of romping about.

clue.text: One set, fumbling inside underwear in Italian city

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go within the item of underwear

parts.note: a bra is an item of women's underwear

indicators.note: fumbling hands get things muddled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: as printed the word is set; the letters needed are those of sec, a likely misprint
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone fumbles under a bra in an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed, set gives a T where the answer needs a C; the clue probably meant sec, so One and that are jumbled inside the bra.
explanation.definitionFit: Brescia is a city in Lombardy, northern Italy.

clue.text: Flow-interrupter attached to party nutter!

parts.note: a weir is a low dam that holds back a river's flow
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Someone attaching a contraceptive to a party animal, the crackpot.
explanation.walkthrough: Flow-interrupter hints at something intimate, but it is a dam across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A weirdo is an odd or eccentric person, which nutter also means in British slang.

clue.text: Reversal of Blair party by a Conservative political clique?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: Blair's party name is read backwards

parts.note: Tony Blair led the Labour Party, abbreviated LAB

explanation.surface: A Tory faction turns a Labour shindig on its head.
explanation.walkthrough: Party looks like a celebration, but it is the political party, Labour.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabal is a small secret group of plotters, often in politics.

clue.text: Where to send the unwanted member: Howard's no. 2

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body

indicators.note: the second letter of Howard's name is the one taken

parts.note: Michael Howard's surname, whose second letter is taken

explanation.surface: Michael Howard's deputy is the unwanted Tory to be sent away.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Howard led the Conservatives in 2005, so his number two looks like a deputy; it is just a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbo is a state of neglect or oblivion where unwanted things are left forgotten.

clue.text: Piss taken by medical staff?

definitions.meaning: surface reading: mocked, as in taking the piss, British slang for teasing
setter's reading: urine literally collected by doctors or nurses for testing

explanation.walkthrough: Taking the piss is British slang for mockery, so the clue reads as doctors teasing someone; literally it is a urine sample.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is a sample, of urine for instance, taken for medical testing.

clue.text: Lot of dollars injected into leaderless Conservative party out of control

indicators.note: the money goes inside the beheaded party word
losing its leader means dropping the first letter

parts.note: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party
G is a grand, a thousand dollars

explanation.surface: Cash poured into a Tory party with no leader leaves it out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is a wild, unrestrained party, often of sexual excess.

clue.text: Naomi's right out of place in the old town's starry group

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city, the crossword's favourite old town

indicators.note: letters that are out of place need rearranging

parts.note: the name with its 's, used letter by letter

explanation.surface: Naomi Campbell's right to be among the stars of the old home town.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursa Minor, the Little Bear, is a constellation, a group of stars that includes Polaris.

clue.text: Suffer hot dog

parts.note: in and hot both mean fashionable
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.walkthrough: Hot dog looks like the sausage snack, but it splits into two separate words.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty is to suffer it or bring it on oneself.

clue.text: Tabloid young lover of Conservative leader's last to go, flipping lout

indicators.note: the letter going is dropped from the party word
the last letter of the word leader is the one that goes

parts.note: the word leader itself, whose final letter is taken

indicators.note: flipping turns the slang word for a lout the other way round

parts.note: a yob is a British word for a loutish youth

explanation.surface: A red-top story about a Tory leader's young lover, a flipping lout.
explanation.walkthrough: Leader's last means the last letter of leader, not the end of the party name; flipping is both a mild British curse and the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Toyboy is a tabloid word for a much younger male lover of an older woman.

clue.text: College's onto sporty simultaneous coupling

indicators.note: the college comes first, placed onto the sporty word

parts.note: a poly was a British polytechnic college
gamy means spirited or plucky, game for anything

explanation.surface: A college bonding over sport and coupling up all at once.
explanation.walkthrough: A poly was a British polytechnic, a kind of college.
explanation.definitionFit: Polygamy is marriage to more than one spouse at the same time, so plural concurrent unions.
